editorial:
Imagine you are looking back at your own childhood and wondering why your parents acted the way they did. You will follow Jack, a boy growing up in Texas during the 1950s, as he deals with a strict father and a loving mother. It feels less like a normal story and more like a dream or a memory. One minute you are seeing a family dinner, and the next, you are seeing the birth of the entire universe. It is a very calm and thoughtful experience that asks big questions about where we come from and why we are here.

The acting is great because it feels real and not forced. You should know that the pace is very slow, and there is not much of a plot, so do not expect a fast movie with big twists. If you love beautiful shots and a peaceful mood, you will love this.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a dream-like sequence on a beach where the adult Jack finally finds peace. He sees his parents and his siblings as they were in the past. This shows that he has finally forgiven his father and made peace with his childhood. He realizes that everyone struggles and that love is the most important thing. He lets go of his sadness and finds a sense of calm and faith in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves thinking about life and seeing beautiful art.
